shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Cross-level combat, senses, NPC travel, CE bridge (experimental), "Traveler" climb animations, blueprint art, wall risers, research-gated links, a per-colony off switch, Perspective Shift + Toggleable Overlays support. Window 12 adds cross-level ability/jump targeting (§82), band-aware range/target overlays (§83) and cross-level AI jumping (§84, unverified).

> **⚠⚠ V1 SOURCE IS NOT GONE. DATED SOURCE BACKUPS LIVE AT `D:\Rimworld\As above, So below\<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>\Source\`** (ten snapshots, newest `20260726-154207`). These are `Source/` only - no Defs, no Textures. **When a V2 feature has a V1 ancestor, READ THE V1 FILE FIRST.** Confirmed useful: `Source/Stairs/ClimbAnimation.cs` (§78d). **What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity.

**⚠⚠ THE FIFTY-FOUR RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): **NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE** - see rule 54 for the grep version. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE - selectable is drawable, and so is **highlightable** (§83). 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW. 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL. 43 (§78): **DEFER THE MOVE, NEVER THE DECISION.** 44 (§78b): AN OFFSET APPLIED WHOLE ON FRAME ONE IS A TELEPORT. 45 (§78d): **A DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOT A DIRECTION OF ELEVATION.** 46 (§78d): **NON-UNIFORM SCALE x ROTATION = SHEAR.** 47 (§79): **A FOREIGN MOD'S CACHED CURSOR CELL IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT COORDINATE SPACE.** 48 (§81a): **A WRITE THAT IS READ BACK BY ITS OWN CALLER IS NOT A WRITE.** 49 (§0c): **A TEST THAT PROVES FEATURE A SAYS NOTHING ABOUT FEATURE B, AND "TESTS GOOD" IS NOT A SCOPE.** 50 (§82a): **TWO OF OUR OWN PATCHES ON ONE VANILLA METHOD CANCEL SILENTLY.** Harmony hands a POSTFIX the arguments AS THE PREFIX LEFT THEM. **GREP OUR OWN `[HarmonyPatch(...)]` LIST FOR THE TARGET METHOD BEFORE ADDING A PATCH TO IT.** 51 (§82b): **A FACTORY HAS USUALLY CONSUMED ITS INPUT BY THE TIME THE POSTFIX RUNS.** `PawnFlyer.MakeFlyer` despawns the pawn before returning it; capture in a PREFIX via `__state`. 52 (§83a): **AN OVERLAY MUST ASK THE SAME QUESTION THE CLICK WILL ASK, AND IT MUST NOT BE A QUESTION THAT WRITES.** `Verb.CanHitTargetFrom` funnels into our shoot-line patch, which ends in `ABCombatRelay.RecordSolution`; call the pure solver underneath. **Observers do not write.** 53 (§83c): **A PREDICATE PASSED IN IS CLOSED OVER THE ARGUMENTS THE CALLER ALREADY HAS.** 54 (§84a): **A CLEAN GREP IS NOT AN ABSENCE - SEARCH FOR THE CAPABILITY, NOT THE TYPE NAME.** Vanilla parameterises AI ability behaviour through an `AbilityDef` FIELD on generic job givers configured in ThinkTree XML, so `Verb_Jump|JumpUtility|CastJump|JumpRange` matched ZERO AI files and produced a confident, wrong "vanilla has no AI jumping" that was reported to the user. **When a grep returns nothing, widen to the concept - `ls` the `JobGiver_*` files, grep the Defs for the class - before concluding the behaviour does not exist.**

# 84. CROSS-LEVEL AI JUMPING — WINDOW 12, BUILT, **NOT FIELD-VERIFIED**

`Source/V2/ABBandLeapAI.cs` + `Defs/V2/AB_ThinkTrees.xml`.

**⚠⚠ 84a. THE CORRECTION THAT STARTED IT (rule 54).** Told the user "vanilla has NO AI path for jumping at all", from a grep for `Verb_Jump|JumpUtility|CastJump|JumpRange` that returned seven files and no JobGiver. **Vanilla has three AI jump givers**; every one reaches jumping through an `AbilityDef` FIELD, so none matched:
* `JobGiver_AIJumpEscapeEnemies` - Core `Abilities_Escape` tree, for anyone with `Longjump` (the `LongjumpLegs` gene ⇒ every sanguophage): panic-jump when damaged past 25%, harmed within 120 ticks, under close combat pressure with 2+ threats within 2 cells.
* `JobGiver_AIJumpToJobTarget` + `JobGiver_AIJumpToJobRescueTarget` - Biotech `SubTrees_Mech.xml`, for `LongjumpMechLauncher`: jump to beat a fire, jump to rescue a downed pawn (targetIndex A, then B for the bed).
Both vanilla trees gate on `ThinkNode_ConditionalColonist` with `invert=true`, i.e. **vanilla deliberately keeps AI ability use away from colonists.**

**84.2 PART A - THE MECH GIVER REPAIR.** `JobGiver_AIJumpToJobTarget` gates on `pawn.Position.DistanceTo(result)` vs range plus a flat `GenSight.LineOfSight`, BEFORE it consults `ValidateTarget` (band-aware since §82) - the mod's most common defect, sixth instance. Prefix reimplements the body band-aware for cross-band targets only. **⚠ AND THE SECOND HALF WAS A LANDMINE:** vanilla then calls `RCellFinder.TryFindGoodAdjacentSpotToTouch`, whose filter is `toucher.CanReach(item, ...)` - **a walking question standing in front of a jump** (rule 5). Repairing only the distance test would have moved the failure there and looked like the fix failed. `ABBandLeapAI.TryFindJumpSpotToTouch` replaces it: same 8-way adjacency and `CanReachImmediate`, but legality by `ValidJumpTarget` + `verb.CanHitTargetFrom`, nearest measured BAND-LOCALLY. **⚠ The giver returns null and starts its own job with `resumeCurJobAfterwards: true`** - preserved exactly, or mechs would stop resuming on flat maps.

**84.3 PART B - THE NEW GIVER, AND THE THINK TREE DOES THE HARD PART.** `JobGiver_ABBandLeap` hangs off **`Humanlike_PostDuty`**, vanilla's own modder insertion hook, declared as our own `ThinkTreeDef` with `insertTag`/`insertPriority` - no vanilla def is patched and two mods inserting at the same point cannot collide. A pawn only reaches that tag once its Lord duty produced NO job, so **"the AI wanted to get somewhere and could not" is a structural fact at that point rather than a heuristic to tune**, and an ordinary raid never runs a line of it.

**84.4 THE DECISION, IN ORDER.** Not drafted (a drafted pawn does what the player said; spending a charge for them is the one thing that would read as a bug) → off cooldown → has a usable jump → has a goal → goal is on another band → **cannot walk there** (the conservative gate) → a landing cell exists. **⚠ ABILITY BEFORE APPAREL:** an ability recharges; a jump pack burns one of five charges the AI can never replace (reloading needs chemfuel and a hauling job it will not do).

**⚠ 84.5 THE GOAL HAS FOUR SOURCES AND THE FOURTH IS THE ONLY ONE THAT MATTERS IN THE HEADLINE CASE.** enemyTarget → duty.focus → CurJob.targetA → (hostile to player) the nearest colonist or colony building, measured band-locally. An assaulting raider that cannot reach anything has NO enemy target (acquisition already failed), NO duty focus (AssaultColony states none) and NO job (every giver returned null - which is why we are being asked). Without the fourth source the feature would be inert in exactly the situation it was built for.

**⚠⚠ 84.6 THE REACHABILITY TEST IS FROM THE LANDING CELL, NOT FROM THE PAWN.** `pawn.CanReach` answers a question about where the pawn is standing now, which is useless here - it is *why* we are jumping. `map.reachability.CanReach(landingCell, goal, Touch, TraverseParms.For(pawn))` is the clause that makes the jump worth taking, and it is simultaneously "conservative" and "may not strand a pawn" in one test: a jump is always a shortcut into somewhere useful, never a one-way trip into a sealed room where the stuck watchdog would start firing. Cheap filters (band, gutter, `ValidJumpTarget`, forbidden) run over the whole disc; the expensive pair (shaft solve + reachability) runs over the best **24** by distance-to-goal, selected without sorting or allocating. Cooldowns: **300 ticks** after a failed scan, **600** after a jump.

**84.7 PART C - THE PANIC JUMP IS CLAMPED TO ITS OWN BAND (user's call).** `JobGiver_AIJumpEscapeEnemies` picks its cell with `CellFinderLoose.GetFallbackDest`, a raw-distance search whose only filter is `verb.ValidateTarget` - which since §82 ACCEPTS a cell one level down. Near a seam a cornered sanguophage could panic-jump through the floor, i.e. a stealth breach mechanic arriving by accident through a reflex. A postfix nulls a cross-band escape job; the pawn falls through to the rest of its tree, exactly as on a flat map with no fallback cell.

(2) `AB2: combat report` → `leapAI: scans/leaps/noLanding/escapesClamped/giverRepairs`; `leaps > 0` is the proof. (5) **Confirm colonists never jump on their own** - the drafted carve-out plus vanilla's own colonist exclusion should make this impossible, but it is the regression that would be most annoying in play. (6) Watch for a pawn that jumps, lands, and cannot proceed - §84.6 should make it impossible; if it happens the reachability clause is wrong.
